Hi Kara — great to hear from you and thanks for the files. Short answer: yes, we can support a 3-month staircase to move from 2M -> 4M -> 6M committed tokens, plus a burst cushion. A few notes up front:

- Pricing: we usually apply stepped-commit pricing that averages across the quarter; Ill attach a worked example in the formal SOW.
- Burst behavior: we provide a soft-burst band (configurable) that allows sustained traffic up to 1.5x committed for short periods before we trigger a soft throttle. Soft throttle is token-shed/concurrency-limited (graceful degradation) rather than hard 429s unless the account is in extreme overage for >72h.
- Rate-limits: for your expected peak concurrency we recommend a baseline of 40 tokens/s per API key with autoscaling buckets for short windows; we can tune this during onboarding.

Can you do Wed 10–10:30 PT for a quick sync? Ill invite Ben from Sales and Irene from Platform Ops to cover pricing and SLOs.

Cheers,

Looping through the numbers after Kara's forecast and the Nov usage sheet. Quick internal notes so were aligned for Wed call:

- Current commit: 2,100,000 tokens/month (avg Nov). Proposed committed target: 6,000,000 tokens/month phased over 3 months (2.1M -> 4.05M -> 6.0M).
- Burst cushion: propose a 50% burst pocket on top of each months commit (so month 3 burst ceiling = 9M tokens for short windows). This keeps unit economics reasonable and gives headroom.
- Pricing: recommend a blended rate for Q1 where the staircase averages to ~4.05M in month 1-3 to smooth the per-token price and avoid churn shocks. I can prepare the delta vs current spend.
- Rate limits / operational SLOs: platform ops — Irene, can you confirm safe defaults for Hosted API: 40 tokens/s per key, per-region; with a burst token bucket that allows short spikes up to 60 tokens/s for 5 minutes. After that, soft throttle to 30 tokens/s and queue. Also confirm logging retention and audit captures for any throttle events.

Irene: if those defaults look okay, Ill include them in the negotiated SOW and call them out as "soft throttle behavior" with an operational playbook and a 72h overage window before escalation.

Thanks everyone — good conversation today. Confirming the operational commitments we can include in the SOW and options for the renewal: 

1) Staged commit: 3-month staircase (effective Jan–Mar 2027): 2.1M -> 4.05M -> 6.0M committed tokens. Billing will prorate by calendar month; we will include a worked example in the SOW.
2) Burst pocket: configurable 50% burst on top of each months committed tokens for short windows (defined as any contiguous 6-hour period). Burst beyond the cushion will be handled by soft-throttle (graceful shedding and queueing); we will not issue hard 429s unless there is persistent overage >72 hours.
3) Rate limits: default is 40 tokens/s per API key, per region. Burst token bucket permits 60 tokens/s for rolling 5-minute windows. Soft-throttle floor is 30 tokens/s with queueing; we will expose metrics for throttle events to your team via the Console and push them into the shared SLO dashboard.
4) SLA / Ops: For Dedicated incidents we have a 2-hour P1 response SLA; for Hosted we guarantee 99.5% uptime and 95th %-ile latency targets per the attached annex. Throttle incidents will be marked as operational events and captured in the monthly usage reports.

Next steps for Kara / Procurement: please confirm (a) approval to proceed with the staircase commit and (b) whether legal needs additional redlines. We can push the SOW and DocuSign link once you confirm.

Regards,
Irene Choi
Platform Operations Lead | Redwood Inference
